task.text:
[0] Bmal1 (ARNTL) knockout mice started showing growth retardation at 16-18 weeks of age, and their aging phenotypes were more severe than in control mice of the same age.

[1] BRCA1 heterozygous mice were prone to spontaneous tumorigenesis and had a shorter lifespan than wild type.

[2] Irradiated BRCA1 heterozygous mice didn't have lifespan differences from irradiated wild-type mice, but had 96.4% tumor occurrence.

[3] Heterozygous TP53BP1 knockout does not rescued BRCA1 mutant mice from senescence, although it does protect against intrauterine death.

[4] TP53BP1 deletion rescued mice from intrauterine death, premature aging, senescence, and cell death, caused by the BRCA1 mutation without significantly increasing the rates of tumorgenesis. It is not possible to determine the average lifespan of mice because the authors did not wait for them to die.

[5] The increase in life span was associated with attenuated tumor development P <0.001 (fig 3b).

[6] Lifespans of BubR1H/H (hypomorphic) and SIRT2tg/BubR1H/H were compared (fig 4), P = 0.0384. According to the article max lifespan was extended by 21%.

[7] Lifespans of BubR1H/H (hypomorphic) and SIRT2tg/BubR1H/H were compared (fig 4), P = 0.004.

[8] Lifespans of BubR1H/H (hypomorphic) and SIRT2tg/BubR1H/H were compared (fig 4), P = 0.7915

[9] Bub3/Rae1 haploinsufficient mice manifest aging-related phenotypes and shortened lifespan (p<0.05). Haploinsufficiency of Bub3 and Rae1 separately didn't cause these effects, suggesting synergy between Bub3 and Rae1.

Each numbered passage describes one lifespan experiment. For each, report three things using ONLY that passage:
  organism: the model organism studied, one lowercase word
  direction: exactly one of 'increases lifespan', 'decreases lifespan', or 'no change'
  method: how the gene was altered, e.g. gene knockout, overexpression, mutation, knockdown

Output one block per passage, in order, formatted exactly:
[0]
organism: ...
direction: ...
method: ...

Nothing else. If a passage does not state something, write 'unstated'.
